title: Can a Pay Rise Leave You Worse Off? The 58p Truth 💷 #shorts
description:
Go £1 over the higher-rate line and you still keep 58p of it.

Only income above £50,270 is taxed at 40%. Add 2% National Insurance above the Upper Earnings Limit and you keep 58p of every extra £1.

Where it really bites: between £100,000 and £125,140 your Personal Allowance tapers away (£1 for every £2), so that band is taxed at an effective 60%. And the High Income Child Benefit Charge starts at £60,000, with all of it repaid by £80,000.

Sources: gov.uk/income-tax-rates · gov.uk/national-insurance-rates-letters · gov.uk/child-benefit-tax-charge

2026/27 rates for England, Wales and Northern Ireland (Scotland's income tax bands differ). Ignores student loans and pension contributions. General education, not financial advice.
